filas_sql.title: POWERING AGRICULTURE: PRESENT STATUS, FUTURE POTENTIAL, AND CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY APPLICATIONS
filas_sql.abstract: MODERN AGRICULTURE REQUIRES MUCH GREATER ENERGY INPUT THAN CONVENTIONAL AGRICULTURE, WHICH HEAVILY DEPENDS ON FOSSIL FUELS FOR DRYING GRAIN, MANUFACTURING FERTILIZERS, DRIVING MACHINERY, AND GENERATING ELECTRICITY USED FOR HEATING AND LIGHTING PURPOSES. THESE ENERGY-INTENSIVE ACTIVITIES AT OR OFF THE FARM LEVEL ARE MAJOR CONTRIBUTORS TO GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) EMISSIONS. IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES, THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR 35% OF GHG EMISSIONS, WHILE THIS FIGURE IS ONLY 12% IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES. HOWEVER, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ITS IMPACT CAN BE ALLEVIATED BY PROMOTING RENEWABLE ENERGY (RE) IN AGRICULTURAL APPLICATIONS, SUCH AS SOLAR, WIND, HYDRO-POWERED WATER PUMPS, GREENHOUSE HEATING AND COOLING, SOLAR WATER HEATERS, SOLAR DRYERS FOR POST-HARVEST PROCESSING, AND LIGHTING TECHNOLOGIES. NEVERTHELESS, TRANSFORMING FROM A NON-RENEWABLE ENERGY-BASED SYSTEM TO A RENEWABLE-BASED AGRICULTURE SYSTEM IMPOSES SEVERAL CHALLENGES. RE TRANSITION SHOULD BE IMMEDIATE AND ORDERLY, AND REQUIRES INCENTIVE-BASED POLICIES FOR BOTH LOWER- AND HIGHER-INCOME COUNTRIES. THIS STUDY INVESTIGATES THE APPLICATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGIES FOR AGRICULTURAL ACTIVITIES FOR DEVELOPING AND DEVELOPED COUNTRIES, AND REVEALS THE PRESENT STATUS AND FUTURE POTENTIAL ALONG WITH CHALLENGES TO BE FACED IN THIS SECTOR. THE RESULTS SUGGEST THAT RENEWABLE ENERGY APPLICATION IN AGRICULTURE IS WELL ADOPTED IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES. IN CONTRAST, DEVELOPING COUNTRIES ARE STILL STRUGGLING TO APPLY RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN AGRICULTURE FOR CHALLENGES SUCH AS TECHNICAL AND ECONOMIC ONES, AND RE APPLICATION IN AGRICULTURE COULD BE THE KEY TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE SECTOR DEVELOPMENT. RELATED POLICY IMPLICATIONS ARE INDICATED. © 2022 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

gold_bd: ECONOMIC, ENERGY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF ALCOHOL DEHYDRATION TECHNOLOGY ON BIOFUEL PRODUCTION FROM BROWN ALGAE
resultados.respuesta: El artículo más citado publicado en 2015 es "ECONOMIC, ENERGY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF ALCOHOL DEHYDRATION TECHNOLOGY ON BIOFUEL PRODUCTION FROM BROWN ALGAE". Este estudio evalúa el impacto de la tecnología de recuperación de alcohol en los aspectos económicos, consumo energético y ambiental de la producción de bioetanol a partir de algas pardas. El proceso considerado es la digestión anaeróbica de algas pardas para producir ácidos grasos volátiles (VFAs), que luego son hidrogenados para producir alcoholes mezclados. Se analizan tres procesos alternativos, es decir, la combinación de evaporación/destilación híbrida (PV), vapor-permeación/destilación híbrida (VP) y destilación clásica con membranas moleculares (CLASICO), para la deshidratación y recuperación de etanol. Las alternativas se analizan en términos de valor del producto (por ejemplo, precio de venta mínimo de etanol – MESP), costos de capital, consumo energético y huella de carbono. Para una escala de planta de 400,000 toneladas/año de alga seca, los MESP para el proceso PV, VP y CLASICO fueron calculados en $1.06/GAL, $1.08/GAL y $1.24/GAL, respectivamente. Los resultados muestran que los procesos PV, VP y CLASICO tienen costos de servicios públicos anuales de $2.0, $2.6 y $4.6 millones, respectivamente, para la recuperación de alcoholes y producen 23.1, 30.2 y 62.2 Kton CO<INF>2</INF>-EQ/año de gases de efecto invernadero. Por lo tanto, el proceso PV es más económico y ambientalmente amigable, con un MESP más bajo, emisiones de CO<INF>2</INF> más bajas y requisitos de servicios públicos más bajos. Un análisis de sensibilidad indica que el precio de venta de los alcoholes más pesados y el precio de la biomasa tienen el mayor impacto en la economía de la producción de bioetanol a partir de algas pardas. Este artículo aborda temas como la producción de bioetanol, tecnologías de deshidratación, costos económicos y ambientales, y la optimización de procesos para una producción más sostenible y rentable.

filas_sql.title: ECONOMIC, ENERGY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF ALCOHOL DEHYDRATION TECHNOLOGY ON BIOFUEL PRODUCTION FROM BROWN ALGAE
filas_sql.abstract: THIS STUDY EVALUATES THE IMPACT OF ALCOHOL RECOVERY TECHNOLOGY ON THE ECONOMICS, ENERGY CONSUMPTION, AND ENVIRONMENT OF BIOETHANOL PRODUCTION FROM BROWN ALGAE. THE PROCESS UNDER CONSIDERATION IS THE ANAEROBIC DIGESTION OF BROWN ALGAE TO PRODUCE VFAS (VOLATILE FATTY ACIDS), WHICH ARE THEN HYDROGENATED TO PRODUCE MIXED ALCOHOLS. THREE ALTERNATIVE PROCESSES, I.E., HYBRID PERVAPORATION/DISTILLATION (PV), HYBRID VAPOR-PERMEATION/DISTILLATION (VP), AND CLASSICAL MOLECULAR-SIEVES/DISTILLATION (CLASSICAL), ARE CONSIDERED FOR THE DEHYDRATION AND RECOVERY OF ETHANOL. THE ALTERNATIVES ARE ANALYZED IN TERMS OF PRODUCT VALUE (I.E., MINIMUM ETHANOL SELLING PRICE – MESP), CAPITAL COSTS, ENERGY CONSUMPTION, AND CARBON FOOTPRINT. FOR A PLANT SCALE OF 400,000 TON/YEAR OF DRY BROWN ALGAE, THE MESPS FOR THE PV (PERVAPORATION), VP (VAPOR PERMEATION), AND CLASSICAL PROCESSES WERE CALCULATED TO BE $1.06/GAL, $1.08/GAL, AND $1.24/GAL, RESPECTIVELY. RESULTS SHOW THAT THE PV, VP, AND CLASSICAL PROCESSES HAVE $2.0, $2.6, AND $4.6 MILLION/YEAR UTILITY COSTS, RESPECTIVELY, FOR THE RECOVERY OF ALCOHOLS AND PRODUCE 23.1, 30.2, AND 62.2 KTON CO<INF>2</INF>-EQ/YEAR GREENHOUSE GASES. THEREFORE, PV IS MORE ECONOMICAL AND ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY PROCESS, WITH LOWER MESP, CO<INF>2</INF> EMISSIONS, AND UTILITY REQUIREMENTS. A SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS INDICATES THAT THE SELLING PRICE OF THE HEAVIER ALCOHOLS AND BIOMASS PRICE HAVE THE HIGHEST IMPACT ON THE ECONOMICS OF BIOETHANOL PRODUCTION FROM BROWN ALGAE. © 2017 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

filas_sql.title: POWERING AGRICULTURE: PRESENT STATUS, FUTURE POTENTIAL, AND CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY APPLICATIONS
filas_sql.abstract: MODERN AGRICULTURE REQUIRES MUCH GREATER ENERGY INPUT THAN CONVENTIONAL AGRICULTURE, WHICH HEAVILY DEPENDS ON FOSSIL FUELS FOR DRYING GRAIN, MANUFACTURING FERTILIZERS, DRIVING MACHINERY, AND GENERATING ELECTRICITY USED FOR HEATING AND LIGHTING PURPOSES. THESE ENERGY-INTENSIVE ACTIVITIES AT OR OFF THE FARM LEVEL ARE MAJOR CONTRIBUTORS TO GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) EMISSIONS. IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES, THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR 35% OF GHG EMISSIONS, WHILE THIS FIGURE IS ONLY 12% IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES. HOWEVER, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ITS IMPACT CAN BE ALLEVIATED BY PROMOTING RENEWABLE ENERGY (RE) IN AGRICULTURAL APPLICATIONS, SUCH AS SOLAR, WIND, HYDRO-POWERED WATER PUMPS, GREENHOUSE HEATING AND COOLING, SOLAR WATER HEATERS, SOLAR DRYERS FOR POST-HARVEST PROCESSING, AND LIGHTING TECHNOLOGIES. NEVERTHELESS, TRANSFORMING FROM A NON-RENEWABLE ENERGY-BASED SYSTEM TO A RENEWABLE-BASED AGRICULTURE SYSTEM IMPOSES SEVERAL CHALLENGES. RE TRANSITION SHOULD BE IMMEDIATE AND ORDERLY, AND REQUIRES INCENTIVE-BASED POLICIES FOR BOTH LOWER- AND HIGHER-INCOME COUNTRIES. THIS STUDY INVESTIGATES THE APPLICATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGIES FOR AGRICULTURAL ACTIVITIES FOR DEVELOPING AND DEVELOPED COUNTRIES, AND REVEALS THE PRESENT STATUS AND FUTURE POTENTIAL ALONG WITH CHALLENGES TO BE FACED IN THIS SECTOR. THE RESULTS SUGGEST THAT RENEWABLE ENERGY APPLICATION IN AGRICULTURE IS WELL ADOPTED IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES. IN CONTRAST, DEVELOPING COUNTRIES ARE STILL STRUGGLING TO APPLY RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN AGRICULTURE FOR CHALLENGES SUCH AS TECHNICAL AND ECONOMIC ONES, AND RE APPLICATION IN AGRICULTURE COULD BE THE KEY TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE SECTOR DEVELOPMENT. RELATED POLICY IMPLICATIONS ARE INDICATED. © 2022 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

El grupo de Carsten Agert ha publicado artículos en diversas áreas del conocimiento, según los resultados obtenidos de la consulta SQL y la búsqueda semántica. En particular, uno de los artículos publicados se titula "INFLUENCE OF SPECTRALLY SELECTIVE SOLAR CELLS ON MICROALGAE GROWTH IN PHOTO-BIOREACTORS". Este artículo trata sobre el uso de celdas solares selectivas espectralmente (SSSC) para combinar fotovoltaicos y fotosíntesis. Las SSSC pueden cubrir toda una superficie de terreno, invernaderos o bioreactores foto-bioquímicos, aprovechando la absorción del espectro de clorofila A, que tiene sus máximos en aproximadamente 460 y 680 nm. En este estudio, se presentan las técnicas de compartición espectral de luz solar utilizando celdas solares selectivas basadas en nanoadsorbenes combinadas con la producción de biomasa de microalgas (Acetodesmus obliquus). Estas SSSC se instalaron en una unidad de cultivo de laboratorio para evaluar el impacto de la iluminación espectral selectiva sobre la tasa de crecimiento alga. Se probaron diferentes flujos de fotones y el efecto de la luz azul sobre la producción de biomasa.

Además, de acuerdo con la búsqueda semántica, el grupo ha investigado en áreas como las bacterias patógenas intracelulares (Anaplasma phagocytophilum), la mineralización de nitrógeno y el microambiente en la fermentación de residuos de maíz, el diseño óptimo de producción de metanol renovable con objetivos políticos y conflictos esperados, los costos y beneficios del uso de secadores solares parabólicos para productos de hierbas secas en Tailandia, y las influencias de la sombra sobre la batata dulce leñosa desde perspectivas fisiológicas, fotoquímicas y transcriptómicas. Estos artículos abordan temas tan variados como la biología celular, la ingeniería de procesos, la agricultura sostenible y la biotecnología.

En resumen, el grupo de Carsten Agert ha mostrado una amplia gama de intereses en diferentes campos del conocimiento, publicando artículos que van desde la investigación sobre celdas solares selectivas hasta estudios microbiológicos y análisis de microambientes.

filas_sql.abstract: SPECTRALLY SELECTIVE SOLAR CELLS (SSSC) CAN BE USED TO COMBINE PHOTOVOLTAICS AND PHOTOSYNTHESIS. IN CONTRAST TO AGRIVOLTAIC SYSTEMS WHERE OPAQUE MODULES ARE INSTALLED WITH ENOUGH SPACE IN BETWEEN TO REALIZE ONLY PARTIAL SHADING. SSSCS CAN BE USED TO COVER AN ENTIRE AREA OF FARM LAND, GREENHOUSES OR PHOTO-BIOREACTORS. THIS CONCEPT TAKES ADVANTAGE OF THE CHLOROPHYLL A ABSORPTION SPECTRUM, WHICH EXHIBITS ITS MAXIMA AT AROUND 460 AND 680 NM. A SSSC CAN BE USED TO GENERATE ELECTRICITY BY ABSORBING THE REMAINING GREEN AND INFRARED LIGHT. IN THIS PUBLICATION WE PRESENT THE SPECTRAL SHARING OF SUN LIGHT USING NANO-ABSORBER BASED SPECTRALLY SELECTIVE SOLAR CELLS IN COMBINATION WITH MICROALGAE (ACUTODESMUS OBLIQUUS) BIOMASS PRODUCTION. THESE SSSCS WERE INSTALLED IN A LAB CULTIVATION UNIT TO EVALUATE THE INFLUENCE OF THE SPECTRAL SELECTIVE ILLUMINATION ON THE ALGAE GROWTH RATE. DIFFERENT PHOTON FLUXES AND THE INFLUENCE OF BLUE LIGHT ON THE BIOMASS PRODUCTION WERE TESTED. © 2021 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

filas_sql.title: EFFECTS OF ABOVE-CANOPY PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS ON TRANSPIRATION AND ENERGY PRODUCTION IN A PEAR ORCHARD
filas_sql.abstract: AGRIVOLTAICS IS A NEW APPROACH TO INTEGRATE PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS AND AGRICULTURAL CROPS ON THE SAME LAND UNIT TO SIMULTANEOUSLY PROTECT CROPS FROM DIRECT SOLAR IRRADIANCE AND HARNESS SOLAR ENERGY. THIS STUDY EVALUATED THE EFFECTS OF SHADING CAST BY PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS ON TRANSPIRATION OF PEAR TREES AND ON ENERGY PRODUCTION. TWO CONFIGURATIONS OF STATIC PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS ORIENTED 45° WEST (45W) AND 5° WEST (5W) WERE INSTALLED ABOVE THE TREE CANOPIES AND COMPARED TO AN UNSHADED TREATMENT (CONTROL). THE EXPERIMENT WAS CONDUCTED IN SUMMER 2021-22 AT THE TATURA SMARTFARM (GOULBURN VALLEY, VICTORIA, AUSTRALIA) IN AN EXPERIMENTAL ‘ANP-0118’ ORCHARD – A BLUSH PEAR MARKETED AS LANYA™. DIFFERENT GROWTH STAGES WERE CONSIDERED: A) RAPID VEGETATIVE GROWTH (49-93 DAFB), B) RAPID FRUIT GROWTH (94-124 DAFB), C) PREHARVEST (125-140 DAFB), AND D) POSTHARVEST (141-168 DAFB). TRANSPIRATION WAS MEASURED BY SAP FLOW SENSORS USING THE HEAT PULSE VELOCITY METHOD. DIURNAL DYNAMICS OF TRANSPIRATION SHOWED THAT CONTROL AND 5W TREES ATTAINED MAXIMUM TRANSPIRATION IN LATE AFTERNOON, BETWEEN 1500 TO 1700 H AEST. THE TRANSPIRATION OF 5W TREES DIPPED AROUND SOLAR NOON DUE TO THE SHADE CAST BY THE PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS. THE SHADE CAST BY THE 45W ARRAYS CAUSED A DECLINE IN THE TRANSPIRATION AROUND 1500 H AEST, BEFORE A TRANSPIRATION REDUCTION OCCURRED IN THE CONTROL AND 5W TREATMENTS. THE 5W CONFIGURATION OUTPERFORMED THE 45W ARRAYS WITH 1.8 MWH GREATER ENERGY PRODUCTION DURING THE STUDY PERIOD OF 119 DAYS IN THE FORMER. THIS RESEARCH INDICATED THAT ABOVE-CANOPY PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAYS CAN BE EFFECTIVE TO MITIGATE WATER LOSS OF ‘ANP-0118’ PEARS. © 2024 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

filas_sql.title: RESPONSE OF CUCUMBER PLANTS TO OXYGEN-ENRICHED NUTRIENT SOLUTION UNDER DIFFERENT GREENHOUSE ENVIRONMENTS
filas_sql.abstract: A STUDY WAS PERFORMED TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF SUPPLEMENTAL OXYGEN ON HYDROPONICALLY GROWN CUCUMBER PLANTS (CUCUMIS SATIVUS ‘JAWELL’) UNDER TWO DIFFERENT GREENHOUSE ENVIRONMENTS, A HIGH TECHNOLOGY GREENHOUSE, AND A SOLAR GREENHOUSE. THREE CONCENTRATIONS OF DISSOLVED OXYGEN, 4 MG L-1 (LOW), 8 MG L-1 (MEDIUM), AND 15 MG L-1 (HIGH) WERE MAINTAINED IN THE ROOT ZONE OF THE PLANTS GROWN IN COCOPEAT MEDIA. THE CROP WAS EVALUATED FOR GROWTH, YIELD, AND POSTHARVEST QUALITY PARAMETERS. THE FRUIT YIELD WAS HIGHER IN THE HIGH TECHNOLOGY GREENHOUSE THAN THE SOLAR GREENHOUSE, HOWEVER, THE DIFFERENCE WAS NOT SIGNIFICANT. THE FRUIT YIELD AND QUALITY WERE PROMOTED AT THE OXYGEN CONCENTRATION OF 8 AND 15 MG L-1 AS COMPARED TO 4 MG L-1 IN THE HIGH TECHNOLOGY GREENHOUSE. IN THE SOLAR GREENHOUSE, THE GROWTH AND YIELD WERE IMPROVED WITH THE INCREASED OXYGEN CONCENTRATION; MAXIMUM PLANT GROWTH AND THE HIGHEST FRUIT YIELD WERE OBTAINED WITH 15 MG L-1 FOLLOWED BY 8 MG L-1 OF DISSOLVED OXYGEN. THE POSTHARVEST QUALITY OF CUCUMBERS WAS ASSESSED AT 10°C TEMPERATURE AND 95% RELATIVE HUMIDITY UP TO 29 DAYS AFTER HARVEST. THE CUCUMBERS HARVESTED FROM HIGH TECHNOLOGY GREENHOUSE DEMONSTRATED LOWER DECAY AND BETTER FIRMNESS OVER A LONGER TIME AS COMPARED TO FRUITS HARVESTED FROM THE SOLAR GREENHOUSE. ALSO, THE FRUITS HARVESTED FROM SOLAR GREENHOUSE RECORDED FASTER AND MORE WEIGHT LOSS. OXYGEN ENRICHED MEDIA IN BOTH THE GREENHOUSE ENVIRONMENTS YIELDED FRUITS WITH LONGER SHELF-LIFE RESULTING IN HIGHER FRUIT WEIGHT AND FIRMNESS THROUGHOUT THE OBSERVATION PERIOD. AN ADDITIONAL EXPERIMENT (CUCUMBER ROOT ASSAY) WAS PERFORMED TO QUANTIFY THE LEVEL OF ADVENTITIOUS ROOTING ELICITED BY OXYGEN-ENRICHED SOLUTION. WE FOUND THAT THE SUPPLEMENTAL LEVELS OF DISSOLVED OXYGEN WERE POSITIVELY RELATED WITH THE NUMBER, LENGTH, AND DRY WEIGHT OF ROOTS. © 2021 ELSEVIER B.V., ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

filas_sql.title: ANALYSIS OF TEMPERATURE AND HUMIDITY IN A LARGE-SCALE ASYMMETRIC PLASTIC-COVERED GREENHOUSE WITH A WATER-CONTROLLED BREWED HOT SYSTEM
filas_sql.abstract: IN ORDER TO ADDRESS LOW LAND-USE EFFICIENCY, AN UNFRIENDLY MECHANIZATION ENVIRONMENT, AND OTHER PROBLEMS IN CHINESE SOLAR GREENHOUSES, A NEW, LARGE-SCALE ASYMMETRIC PLASTIC-COVERED TUNNEL WITH A WATER-CONTROLLED BREWED HOT SYSTEM (AN EXPERIMENTAL GREENHOUSE, GH-F) WAS DESIGNED. GH-F IS ORIENTED IN THE EAST-WEST DIRECTION AND HAS A DOUBLE ROOF WITH A WIDE STEEL FRAME. THE SUN PROJECTION ON THE SOUTH AND NORTH ROOF IS 10-12 AND 7-8 M, RESPECTIVELY. IT ALSO HAS A 1×0.5 M2 FERMENTATION GROOVE IN THE NORTH ROOF. THE EXPERIMENT WAS CONDUCTED FROM 15 DECEMBER 2015 AND 5 FEBRUARY 2016. WE COMPARED THE RESULTS BETWEEN A TRADITIONAL BRICK-STRUCTURE GREENHOUSE (GH-D) AND GH-F FOR TEMPERATURE EXCHANGE, HUMIDITY EXCHANGE, AND BUILDING EXPENSES. OUR RESULTS SHOWED THAT GH-F HAD BOTH THERMAL INSULATION AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS. THE HIGHEST TEMPERATURE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN GH-F AND THE ENVIRONMENT WAS 21.9°C DURING WINTER. THE AVERAGE NIGHT AIR TEMPERATURE IN GH-F WAS KEPT ABOVE 8°C, WHICH WAS ONLY 1°C LOWER THAN THAT IN GH-D. THIS DIFFERENCE WAS CONSISTENT DURING CLOUDY AND NON-CLOUDY NIGHTS. TEMPERATURES IN THE GH-F SYSTEM WERE HIGHER THAN THE ENVIRONMENTAL TEMPERATURE, RANGING FROM 11.1 TO 15.3°C DURING NON-CLOUDY NIGHTS, 8.5-11.7°C DURING CLOUDY NIGHTS, AND 12.3-13.7°C DURING SNOWY NIGHTS. HOWEVER, THE SYSTEM TEMPERATURE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN GH-F AND GH-D DURING SNOWY NIGHTS WAS DEPENDENT ON TIME. THE RELATIVE HUMIDITY IN GH-F WAS 2-7% LOWER THAN THAT IN GH-D AT NIGHT. resultados.pregunta: ¿Cómo funciona el secador de invernadero híbrido para tomates estudiado en el corpus?
resultados.respuesta_esperada: Es un secador de invernadero autónomo de convección forzada que integra un sistema fotovoltaico y un colector solar; se evaluó con un modelo térmico y distintos pretratamientos del tomate (el escaldado 15 min aceleró el secado), comparado con el secado al sol.
resultados.respuesta:
El secador de invernadero híbrido para tomates estudiado en el corpus funciona mediante una combinación de energía solar y sistemas fotovoltaicos. Este sistema está diseñado específicamente para procesadores de tomates postcosecha, como se menciona en el artículo principal del corpus titulado "THERMAL ANALYSIS OF PV SYSTEM AND SOLAR COLLECTOR INTEGRATED WITH GREENHOUSE DRYER FOR DRYING TOMATOES". 

El secador utiliza un sistema híbrido que incluye un colector solar y un sistema fotovoltaico. El objetivo es evaluar el rendimiento térmico del secador de convección forzada mixto mediante un modelo matemático. En este proceso, se investigan diferentes tratamientos previos a la deshidratación de los tomates frescos (enteros, en mitades, rebanados, con y sin blanqueado, con y sin azúcar) antes de secarlos. Se identificó que el blanqueado de los tomates en agua caliente durante 15 minutos antes del secado mostró una mayor tasa inicial de deshidratación comparada con los tratamientos no blanqueados.

El análisis térmico del secador híbrido reveló que la ganancia útil de calor oscilaba entre un 6.45% y un 26.62% de la insolación disponible sobre el secador. El promedio de ganancia de calor diaria utilizada para deshidratar tomates dentro del secador disminuyó del 60% al principio hasta el 5% al final del proceso de secado. La eficiencia general del secador híbrido alcanzó un máximo del 17.96%.

Este sistema permite no solo una deshidratación eficiente, sino también una reducción en las emisiones de carbono y la creación de cero residuos, como se describe en el artículo titulado "PERFORMANCE OF A SOLAR GREENHOUSE-BIOGAS HYBRID DRYER FOR DEHYDRATION OF WATER HYACINTH (EICCHORNIA CRASSIPES)". Este estudio demuestra que este tipo de secadores híbridos son una tecnología de bajo costo y simple, adecuada para pequeños negocios.

Además, el secado solar mejora la recuperación de nutrientes y permite que el digestato se clasifique como fertilizante orgánico (NPK) según las regulaciones europeas. Este tratamiento es efectivo para aumentar la eficiencia del proceso de deshidratación y reducir el impacto ambiental negativo asociado con el almacenamiento y aplicación en tierras del digestato no tratado.

resultados.respuesta:
El estudio sobre el secador solar de invernadero en Filipinas, presentado en el artículo "DESIGN OF A CONTROL SYSTEM FOR GREENHOUSE SOLAR DRYER" (J FINANC, 2023), diseña un sistema de control que incluye:

1. Control de temperatura para minimizar riesgos de salud.
2. Relación entre la humedad y el sensor de carga, utilizando un actuador lineal y una guía lineal para expulsar las bandejas de productos una vez alcanzado el peso requerido basado en su contenido de humedad.
3. Utilización de un controlador proporcional-integral-derivativo (PID) para maximizar la eficiencia del uso del secador y optimizar el tiempo de secado.

Este sistema permite aumentar la flexibilidad del secador solar de invernadero y reducir los riesgos asociados con las altas temperaturas.
